correctness.rationale: For every p,q at least two, an empty column forces weight at least 2p, while full row and column support makes all positive labels reducible to 1. The incidence graph then has no K2 components, at most min(p,floor((p+q)/3)) components, and at least p+q-c edges; a bipartite forest construction attains equality. In the square case equality forces every component a tree of size at least three. The bipartite Cayley tree count and excess-vertex component classification produce all three exact congruence-class formulas. Direct exhaustive labels in five small rectangles, binary subsets for n=2,3,4, and independent coefficient-DP checks n=2,...,10 agreed. The infinite proof does not rely on finite data.

value.rationale: The complete minimum-set census for a classical n-by-n rook board is a naturally motivated extremal enumeration question, distinct from merely calculating a domination number. A forest bijection classifies all optimizers; a nontrivial exact exponential generating coefficient and three explicit formulas reveal distinct residue-dependent configuration counts for every n. These data can support further enumerative, symmetry-quotient and random-optimum studies and are not obtained by renaming a known table.
